scope: File-domain data-cache authority; no SMB CREATE cache grants or NFS delegations enabled. Wire break/ACK integration and full compatibility remain open.
sanitizers: Linux Clang ASan/UBSan/LSan, including real taucloud_file subprocess
checks: authenticated actor/space/path/open ownership and exact acquisition-cookie checks
duplicate acquisition retains cookie; stale cookies and unsolicited ACK rejected
independent files do not recall each other
SMB and core conflicts wait for holder writes/flush/ACK; later reads see final contents
NFS read/write handle resolution triggers native break; the same mutation request can succeed after ACK
external native opens cause recall without occupying the file-domain dispatcher
short authority expiry fences complete open; fresh polling cannot extend a five-second break
close, explicit release, revocation and SMB recovery clean up exclusion; delete-pending acquisition declined
actual file worker with no incoming IPC autonomously releases native exclusion, rejects old-handle writes, and stops cleanly

curl.version: curl 8.5.0 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/8.5.0 OpenSSL/3.0.13 zlib/1.3 brotli/1.1.0 zstd/1.5.5 libidn2/2.3.7 libpsl/0.21.2 (+libidn2/2.3.7) libssh/0.10.6/openssl/zlib nghttp2/1.59.0 librtmp/2.3 OpenLDAP/2.6.10

checks: M2 file schema migrates transactionally with backups; supervisor adds the new DAV role key
TLS Basic auth, UTF-8 names, recursive collection COPY/MOVE/DELETE and type-changing overwrite
independent curl TLS upload/download with certificate verification
auth/condition before 100-continue; ranges, HEAD, 304/412/416; interrupted PUT releases quota
chunk framing, UTF-8/NFC and encoded traversal checks, bounded depth, DTD/entity rejection, destination origin confinement
durable recursive COPY journal resumes from pre-publication crash cut
persistent properties and exclusive lock survive file-worker crash; owner/token enforcement across DAV and core; expiry
share exposure updates revoke active DAV writes and cancellation releases reservations
offline backup refuses running services; restore into new state rotates TLS/IPC, revokes sessions and preserves metadata/files

test_note: The first real-worker probe incorrectly used the SMB role for ping and was denied by the existing IPC policy. The test now uses the supervisor role; no production access rule was changed.
